learning_outcomes.text: Participants understand the development of mobile robots as the development of a mechatronic overall system. They can recognize specific solutions from natural models and methodically integrate them into product development.
Students understand the derivation of bionic concepts and can implement them in technical applications.
Students are able to select suitable components for positioning tasks and fundamentally develop motor controls.
Students can mathematically describe the pose of a mobile robot and apply basic image processing methods.

syllabus_topics: Structural optimization according to natural principles
Sensors for attitude control of robot systems
Development of digital motor controls with current and position control
Real-time firmware for digital motor controls with PWM-based power stages
Control methods for DC, stepper, and BLDC motors
assessment_rules: The module grade for MECB410B is the equally weighted average of the grades from MECB411B and MECB413B. The prerequisite for the exam is the project work or a presentation on the topic of image processing.
